index.title: Pixel Home: cozy queue-sorting puzzles
index.description: Pixel Home is a cozy pixel-art puzzle about getting everyone home. 320 gardens in twenty-two worlds, a story for every pip, a fresh daily puzzle and no timers.
index.tagline: Sort the colors, mind the queue and get every pip home. A cozy pixel-art puzzle for iPhone and iPad.
index.play: Or try the Meadow and today's Daily Flow in your browser.
index.shotTitle: The Pixel Home title screen with lives, the shop, gifts and postcards
index.shotAdventure: Posy’s adventure begins with a story told in pixel panels
index.shotGarden: My Garden: homes, trees and the pips who live there
index.shotLevel: A Cloud Gardens garden: homes, their orders and the Flow Line
index.shotPostcards: Pixel Postcards revealed one piece per cleared level
index.clip: Scan the code with your iPhone camera to open the Pixel Home App Clip: today's Daily Flow in seconds, with nothing to install. If you like it, the full game is one tap away.
index.clipQrAlt: QR code that opens the Pixel Home App Clip
index.how1: Little critters called pips wait in their burrows. Tap one to send it out. If its home is ready, it walks straight there. If not, it waits in the Flow Line, and the line moves strictly first in, first out.
index.how2: Homes take one color at a time and the line is short, so the order you choose is the whole puzzle. Plan it, keep the line moving and fill every home.
index.pipsIntro: Six little pips live in the gardens, each with a color, a symbol and a habit of their own. Every pip and home carries its symbol, so you never have to tell colors apart by hue alone.
index.posyTrait: The welcomer · rose, with a heart
index.posyStory: Posy grew up in the rose hedge at the edge of the Meadow and hasn’t missed a homecoming since. The little heart on top beats faster every time a pip reaches its own front door, and after a good Trio it glows for the rest of the day.
index.dewTrait: The patient one · blue, with a drop
index.dewStory: Dew arrived at Brookside with the first rain and liked the sound of the water too much to leave. While the others fidget in the Flow Line, Dew hums along with the brook, happy to wait a turn. The droplet on top catches the morning light.
index.sprigTrait: The explorer · green, with a leaf
index.sprigStory: Sprig sprouted from a seed someone dropped on a garden path and has been poking into every corner ever since. The two leaves on top twitch whenever something new is near: a switch to turn, a Nook to peek into, a path nobody has walked yet.
index.sunnyTrait: The bright spark · golden, with a star
index.sunnyStory: Sunny found a crown of sunbeams on the Starlit Summit and hasn’t taken it off once. Cheerful, loud and just a little bit of a show-off, Sunny loves a long Flow more than anything, and the crown glints whenever one gets going.
index.lunaTrait: The night owl · plum, with a moon
index.lunaStory: Luna sleeps through the busy part of the day, curled up in a Nook, and wakes when the moon comes up. The glowing orb on Luna’s antenna lights the paths of the Moonlit gardens, so no pip ever has to find home in the dark.
index.cinderTrait: The brave one · amber, with a flower
index.cinderStory: Cinder came down from Ember Ridge, warm as a hearth and twice as quick. Those pointed ears can hear a switch turn from across the garden. Tucked away somewhere, Cinder keeps a pressed flower from the Meadow, to remember the very first home.
index.adventures: Each pip also has an adventure of its own: eight gardens and a finale, its story told in little pixel panels. Every friend you make leaves a keepsake in your garden.
index.garden: Every star you earn is yours to spend in My Garden, the plot behind the title screen: houses, trees and lanterns from every world, paths, ponds and flower beds. The pips you send home live there among what you place and wear the scarves and bow ties you earn. Awards bring gifts like a fountain or a golden pip, and you can share a picture of it all. Garden visits: share a link, and a friend can look around your garden.
index.worlds: From the Meadow to the Bamboo Grove, new ideas arrive gently: switches that redirect the path, Nooks where a pip can rest, color gates, a Stretch that lends you one more slot, and Skippers who cut in line. Clear one of the first ten worlds and it opens again by moonlight, with harder gardens on paths you know. New gardens arrive every week or two, without waiting for an update.
index.daily: The Daily Flow is a new garden each day, the same for every player, with its own leaderboard. Missed a day? Play any of the last 30 from the calendar, and share your result with friends. Every week, the Grand Flow brings one big garden with a leaderboard of its own.
index.wander: Once the third world is cleared, Wander opens: an endless path of gardens, the same for every player, that slowly get harder. It never costs a life, and a leaderboard shows how far everyone has wandered.
index.pace: No level timers. Undo, hints and rewinding to the last solvable moment are always free.
index.lives: A life is used only when you give up a jammed attempt at a new level. Replays, Challenge runs and the Daily Flow never cost one.
index.collect: Earn up to three stars per garden, reveal Pixel Postcards piece by piece, claim a daily gift, finish daily missions, collect rewards for streaks and gardener levels, and unlock new garden looks. A monthly stamp card, a weekly journey and a gift when you come back.
index.devices: Sign in with Apple to keep your garden in iCloud and continue on any iPhone or iPad. Game Center leaderboards and achievements are there if you want them. Widgets, Shortcuts and a Live Activity keep your garden a glance away, and on iPad it plays in landscape too.
index.free1: Pixel Home is free to play. Optional in-app purchases offer extra lives, 24 hours of unlimited lives, Stretch boosters, the Garden Pass (unlimited lives and no ads, for good) and a Supporter Pack, a small thank-you with pieces for your garden.
index.free2: We collect no data that identifies you, and ads are never personalized for players under 16. Read the privacy policy, or visit support if you need a hand.

support.title: Pixel Home support
support.description: Help with Pixel Home: lives, purchases, saving progress, Game Center and how to get in touch.
support.heading: Support
support.lead: Answers to the common questions, and how to reach us.
support.contact: Tell us what happened, which device and iOS version you use, and the version shown at the bottom of the game's Settings.
support.lives: You have five lives, and one comes back every 30 minutes. A life is used only when an attempt at a level you haven't cleared jams and you then restart or leave it. Undo, hints, rewind, replays of cleared levels, Challenge runs and the Daily Flow never cost a life.
support.ads: From version 1.1, a short ad appears after every fifth level you clear, never during one. When you are out of lives you can also choose to watch a video for one, up to three a day. No ad is shown between levels while unlimited lives are running. If you were asked for your consent, you can change your answer under Settings, then Ad choices.
support.stuck: Use Hint for the next useful move. If the flow jams, Rewind takes you back to the last position that can still be solved. Both are free and unlimited.
support.purchase1: Close and reopen the game. A purchase that was interrupted is delivered when the game starts.
support.purchase2: Open the shop and tap Restore purchases. Life packs, unlimited lives and boosters are used up when bought, so there is nothing to restore later, but this collects anything still waiting.
support.purchase3: With Ask to Buy, the items arrive once the purchase is approved.
support.purchase4: For refunds, use reportaproblem.apple.com. Purchases are handled by Apple.
support.progressTitle: Keeping progress on a new device
support.progress1: Open your profile (the gardener badge on the title screen) and choose Sign in with Apple. Your progress is then saved to your own iCloud and follows you to any iPhone or iPad signed in to the same Apple Account with iCloud turned on. Syncing can take up to a minute.
support.progress2: The five regenerating lives belong to each device. Bought and earned lives travel with your save.
support.gameCenter: Game Center is optional. Nothing happens until you tap Sign in to Game Center in your profile. If that says to sign in in the Settings app, open Settings, then Game Center, and sign in there first.
support.delete: In your profile, Delete account data removes the cloud save linked to your Apple Account and signs you out. Deleting the app removes your progress and settings from the device. Your lives and what your purchases granted are kept in the iOS Keychain, so they are still there if you install the game again. To stop using Sign in with Apple with Pixel Home, open the Settings app, tap your name, then Sign in with Apple.

privacy.title: Pixel Home privacy policy
privacy.description: What Pixel Home does with data. From version 1.1 the game shows ads delivered by Google, never personalized for players under 16. From version 1.2 it sends anonymous play statistics that you can turn off.
privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: We do not collect any data that identifies you. Pixel Home has no accounts on our side, and we run no servers for it. From version 1.1 the game shows ads. They are delivered by Google, which receives some information from your device to do that; the sections on advertising below say what, when, and what you can choose. Up to version 1.4 the ads are never personalized and the game never asks to track you. From version 1.5 it asks once for your year of birth and keeps only an age group on your device; only players 16 and over are asked for permission to track, and only their ads may be personalized. From version 1.2 the game also sends anonymous play statistics, which you can turn off; the section on them says what they contain.
privacy.device: Your progress and settings are stored on your device. Your lives, the record of what your purchases granted and your sign-in are kept in the iOS Keychain on your device, where they can remain after the game is deleted, so that they are still there if you install it again. None of this is sent to us.
privacy.signIn: You can play as a guest. If you choose to sign in, the game asks Apple only for your name, never your email address. Apple gives the game an identifier for your account. It is kept on your device and used to label your save in your own iCloud storage. We have no server, so neither the identifier nor your name ever reaches us.
privacy.icloud: When you are signed in, your progress is saved to your own iCloud key-value storage so it can follow you to your other devices. That storage belongs to your Apple Account. We cannot read it. Apple's handling of it is covered by Apple's privacy policy.
privacy.gameCenter: If you choose to sign in to Game Center, your scores and achievements are sent to Apple's Game Center under your Game Center profile. The game does not start Game Center until you ask for it.
privacy.purchases: In-app purchases are processed by Apple. We never see your payment details.
privacy.ads: From version 1.1, Pixel Home shows two kinds of ad, both delivered by Google AdMob: a full-screen ad after every fifth level you clear, and a video you can choose to watch for an extra life. Ads never appear during a level. Version 1.0 shows no ads and contains no advertising software. Nothing is sent to Google until an ad is first needed: when you ask for a video, or shortly before the first ad between levels.
privacy.adsData: To deliver ads, limit how often they appear and measure them, Google's advertising software in the game sends Google information such as your IP address (which shows roughly where you are), details of your device and the app (model, system version, language, app version), identifiers kept for the app on your device, your device's advertising identifier if you allow tracking (from version 1.5, see below), and whether an ad was shown or tapped. This information goes to Google and its advertising partners, not to us. How Google uses information from apps that use its services explains what Google does with it and how you can control it.
privacy.age: From version 1.5 the game asks once, on the title screen after your first cleared level: What year were you born? Only the age group that follows from your answer is kept, on your device: under 13, 13 to 15, or 16 and over. The year itself is never stored, never synced and never sent anywhere, including in the anonymous play statistics. Closing the question without answering counts as under 13. The age group is used only for ads, as the next section explains. You can change it in the game under Settings, then Your age for ads. With the Garden Pass there are no ads, and the question is not asked.
privacy.adsChoice: Up to version 1.4, the game always asks for non-personalized ads. It never asks for permission to track you across other companies' apps and websites, so your advertising identifier is not used. From version 1.5 this depends on the age question. Under 13, or with no answer, nothing changes. From 13 to 15, ads are not marked as directed at children, but as for users under the age of consent in Europe; they are never personalized, and the game never asks to track you. If you are 16 or over, the game shows Apple's request for permission to track once, right after your answer. If you allow it, Google may use your device's advertising identifier, and your ads may be personalized. If you decline, your advertising identifier is not used, but your ads may still be personalized from other information. Ads that are not personalized may still be chosen from general context, such as roughly where you are, your language and the app you are using. If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, Google's consent form asks for your choice before the first ad and lists the advertising partners involved, and ads are personalized only as far as your answer allows. You can refuse, and you can change your answer at any time in the game under Settings, then Ad choices. You can change your answer to Apple's request in the Settings app on your device.
privacy.stats: From version 1.2, Pixel Home sends anonymous play statistics to PostHog, an analytics service: which levels are started, cleared or given up, when lives run out, when the shop is opened and how purchases end, with the app version and the game's language. From version 1.4 they also include whether an ad was watched to the end, closed early or not available, and roughly how many days you have played, in groups such as 2–3 or 8–30. They contain no name, account, advertising or device identifier, and nothing that identifies you: a random value that changes every day lets us count players per day without recognizing anyone from one day to the next. They are stored in the European Union, without IP addresses or location. You can turn them off in the game under Settings, then Share anonymous play statistics. How PostHog handles them is covered by PostHog's privacy policy.
privacy.children: We collect no data that identifies anyone, including children: the play statistics are anonymous. Up to version 1.4, ads are never personalized. From version 1.5, ads for players under 16 are never personalized, and for players under 13, or who did not answer the age question, they are marked as directed at children. For everyone, ads are limited to those Google rates as suitable for general audiences.
privacy.site: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. It uses no cookies and no analytics of its own. GitHub may log technical information such as IP addresses to operate the service, as described in the GitHub privacy statement. From version 1.1 the game also reads a small settings file from this site when it starts, so that it can show fewer ads or say that a new version is available. From version 1.3 it also downloads new gardens from this site, so that new levels can arrive without an update. These requests contain nothing about you, but as with any visit GitHub may log the IP address they come from. You can also play the game in your browser on this site. There it keeps your progress in your browser's storage on your device, and it sends nothing about you or your play to us or anyone else.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new effective date.
privacy.language: This policy is published in several languages for convenience. If the versions differ, the English version applies.
privacy.contact: Questions about this policy can be sent to {email}.
